text: Apple cut revenue guidance after a factory shutdown disrupted production, with revenue falling 8 percent.
Microsoft won a major cloud contract, beating estimates and raising full-year guidance on strong growth.
JPMorgan was downgraded by analysts over concerns about rising credit losses in its lending book.
Exxon Mobil saw revenue fall 6 percent amid weak energy demand and lower oil prices.
Pfizer shares surged after a drug approval was confirmed, lifting the outlook for its pipeline.
Johnson & Johnson held its quarterly dividend steady and reaffirmed profit guidance.
Walmart raised full-year guidance on strong same-store sales growth and record profit.
Chevron posted a gain after announcing a new oil discovery that boosts its reserves.
A data outage disrupted Coca-Cola ordering systems for hours, cutting into shipments.
Procter & Gamble reported record profit and beat earnings estimates on strong demand.
Apple launched a new product that analysts expect to drive strong upgrade demand.
Pfizer faces a lawsuit over allegedly false marketing, raising legal uncertainty.
Microsoft named a new head of its cloud division in a management change.
JPMorgan won a partnership contract, expanding its services business.
Exxon Mobil upgraded after a strong quarter, with profit rising on higher output.
